gloss: to give everything one has; to use up completely

definitions.gloss: to give one's all; to put out everything one has
definitions.explanation: To hold nothing back — to expend all of one's strength, skill, or ideas. Transitive, and most often used of {力|ちから} or {実力|じつりょく} in sports and work.

examples.japanese: {力|ちから}を{出|だ}し{切|き}った。
{練習|れんしゅう}の{成果|せいか}を{出|だ}し{切|き}れなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't fully bring out the results of my practice.

examples.japanese: {最後|さいご}の{試合|しあい}で{実力|じつりょく}を{出|だ}し{切|き}れたので、{負|ま}けても{悔|く}いはない。
examples.english: I was able to give my full ability in the final match, so I have no regrets even though I lost.

notes:
{出|だ}す (to put out) + {切|き}る (the compound-verb suffix meaning to do completely). The {切|き}る ending is what supplies the sense of exhausting the supply.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {力|ちから}を{出|だ}し{切|き}る: to give all one's strength
- {実力|じつりょく}を{出|だ}し{切|き}る: to show one's full ability
- {全|すべ}てを{出|だ}し{切|き}る: to give absolutely everything

USAGE:
The potential negative {出|だ}し{切|き}れない (couldn't give it all) is very common after a disappointing performance.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {使|つか}い{切|き}る: to use up — of supplies and money rather than effort
- {やり切|き}る: to see through to the end — emphasizes finishing the task, not exhausting oneself
